claim: Every public YouTube channel exposes a free RSS feed at videos.xml?channel_id=UC..., but the raw feed only ever returns the 15 most recent uploads.
quote: The raw feed shows 15 videos at a time. YouTube's RSS feed only contains the 15 most recent uploads at any given moment.

claim: The 15-video cap on the channel RSS feed is a hard YouTube limit that third-party services work around to surface more history.
quote: BUT only the most recent 15 videos will be listed!

claim: Native YouTube RSS only shows a handful of recent videos while a channel may have hundreds, so workaround services expand the window up to ~1000 items.
quote: YouTube channels could have hundreds of videos, but only the most recent 10 videos will show up in your feed.

claim: YouTube RSS feeds have propagation latency: a new video can take up to an hour after the WebSub push to actually appear in the feed, and YouTube's WebSub posts are not spec-compliant so they only serve as a re-fetch ping.
quote: YouTube often sends notifications before the entries appear in the feed... up to an hour after the WebSub push... YouTube WebSub posts are not spec compliant and do not contain the required information to send notifications.

claim: yt-dlp's --download-archive records the IDs of downloaded videos and downloads only videos not listed in it; --break-on-existing stops the run on the first archived file; --break-per-input scopes that break (and --max-downloads / --break-match-filters) to each input URL; --flat-playlist lists entries without extracting them.
quote: Download only videos not listed in the archive file... Stop the download process when encountering a file that is in the archive supplied with the --download-archive option... Alters --max-downloads, --break-on-existing, --break-match-filters, and autonumber to reset per input URL

claim: There is a known inconsistency where, with --break-per-input enabled, --break-on-existing breaks per input URL rather than per playlist, introduced by PR #5439.
yt-dlp is the dominant extraction engine these tools wrap, with roughly 169k GitHub stars as of June 2026.

--flat-playlist is used to index a channel/playlist by listing all entries (URLs/IDs/metadata) without downloading, e.g. yt-dlp --flat-playlist --print id, making it the heavier-but-complete alternative to RSS for enumerating an entire channel.
quote: yt-dlp --flat-playlist --print url PLAYLIST_URL to list all video URLs without downloading... --flat-playlist --dump-json to get full metadata without downloading
